parts.label: (i)
parts.official_mark_scheme_text: Find $\angle ABC$ using cosine rule, giving $\cos^{-1}(-\frac18)$, or $2\sin^{-1}(\frac34)$, or $2\cos^{-1}(\frac{\sqrt7}{2})$; or find $\angle BAC=\cos^{-1}(\frac34)$, $\sin^{-1}(\frac{\sqrt7}{4})$, or $\tan^{-1}(\frac{\sqrt7}{3})$. — M1. Guidance: Correct method for $\angle ABC$, expect 1.696 radians awrt; or for $\angle BAC$, expect 0.723 radians awrt. $\angle CBY=\pi-\angle ABC$ or $2\angle CAB$. — M1. Guidance: For attempt at $\angle CBY=\pi-\angle ABC$ or $\angle CBY=2\angle CAB$. OR: find $CY$ from $\triangle ACY$ using Pythagoras or similar triangles. — M1. Guidance: Expect $4\sqrt7$. Then $\angle CBY=\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{8^2+8^2-(\text{their }CY)^2}{2\times8\times8}\right)$. — M1. Guidance: Correct use of cosine rule. $\angle CBY=1.445$ radians AG. — A1. Guidance: Numerical values for angles in radians, if given, need to be correct to 3 decimal places. Method marks can be awarded for working in degrees. Need $82.8^\circ$ awrt converted to radians for A1. Identification of angles must be consistent for A1. Total 3.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.official_mark_scheme_text: Arc $CY=8\times1.445$. — B1. Guidance: Use of $s=8\theta$ for arc $CY$; expect 11.56. $\angle BAC=\frac12(\pi-\angle ABC)$ or $\cos^{-1}(\frac34)$. — *M1. Guidance: For a valid attempt at $\angle BAC$, may be from (i); expect 0.7227 radians. Arc $XC=12\times(\text{their }\angle BAC)$. — DM1. Guidance: Expect 8.673. Perimeter $=11.56+8.673+4=24.2$ cm awrt www. — A1. Guidance: Omission of “+4” only penalised here. Total 4.
